name: Menu Cone
summary: Freehand two-phase selection: the hand points a cone at the target, a pull gesture confirms the candidate set, and the target is picked with a directional gesture from an eight-item marking menu.
howItWorks: Up to eight objects inside the cone are captured when the user pulls the hand back; they appear in a marking menu, and a quick hand movement in the target's direction selects it (direction taken from hand speed exceeding a threshold), with a push gesture to cancel. Using a Kinect and a stereoscopic large display, menu cone (2.17 s) was significantly faster than marker cone (3.85 s) with no difference in errors, had lower physical demand and effort, and was preferred.
advantages: Faster and less tiring than Marker Cone.
Only small, quick hand movements for disambiguation.
limitations: At most eight candidates per menu.

relationships.note: Faster than Marker Cone with similar errors.
Also disambiguates through an out-of-context menu.
